PullRequest.Title: Chat windows follow-ups: proportional resize, keyboard shortcuts, and drag-out/close fixes
PullRequest.Body:
Follow-ups to #345683 for the chat windows of the Agents window (`sessions.chatWindows.enabled`). Regular VS Code layouts are unchanged; the only shared changes are a clamp in `SplitView`'s proportional layout and `Grid.resizeView` accepting a single dimension, which `GridView.resizeView` already did.

## Proportional resize

Resizing a chat window, for example to full screen, used to give all of the change to the last part of each row and column, because `PartGrid` laid out its grid without proportional layout.

- Parts now keep their shares of the window as it is resized. Chrome that isn't a part, such as the title row and the strip, keeps its size.
- The terminals keep their height, as the panel does in the main window. A part can opt in with `IPartGridPartOptions.keepsSize`. `PartGrid` gives it its size back after each layout, and the parts beside it make room in proportion, from unrounded shares, so dragging a window out and back returns the exact sizes.
- `SplitView` clamps a view that keeps its size to its bounds in proportional layout, for example a title row restored at a larger size.
- The preview of where a dragged part goes is laid out proportionally too.

## Keyboard shortcuts in chat windows

- The Changes, Files, Browser and Search Add Tab commands now work in a chat window. They open their tab in the window's main part, so the default and user keybindings to them work there.
- They delegate to a chat window only when invoked from it. Menu entries name their editor group or window, so a click in the main window stays in the main window even while a chat window has focus. Without context arguments, as from a keybinding or the Command Palette, they act on the chat window that has focus.
- F5 (Run) now applies in chat windows, where the Run button shows.
- Cmd+B (Toggle Side Bar) is a no-op in a chat window instead of toggling the main window's side bar.

## Drag-out and close fixes

- **Tabs and splits carried on reopen:** when the chat moves into another window, the chat window reopens the chat's part with its tabs and splits. It captures the part as the chat is about to leave its group.
- **Edge drop:** dropping the chat's group, with the chat alone in it, at the edge of another window moves the chat out instead of closing the chat window.
- **All-or-nothing close:** closing checks every group of the window, including parts created by drops and non-terminal editors in the Terminals part, before anything closes. If the window cannot close, the chat that moved out goes back into its group.
- **No duplicate dirty editors:** editors that ask before closing, such as dirty ones, are left to the close instead of also being moved into the main window, and a captured chat part beside a dirty editor is not reopened.
- **Veto message:** a vetoed move-out, or a vetoed Close Chat Window, says why, as a vetoed editor move does.
- **The chat itself:** the chat counts as still open in another window only where its own editor shows, not an editor that merely matches it.

## Validation

On the final commit (8d42d30b3ad): typecheck, the chat window, chatWindowMoveEditors and sessions terminal suites, and ESLint on the changed files. The last two commits change only `chatWindowService.ts` and its tests; the other suites below ran on the commit before them (52bbaa653d2), with the same base.

New tests cover resizing a chat window out and back in uneven steps in Stacked, so the parts return to their exact sizes. They also cover the Add Tab delegation from keys and menu entries, and the drag-out and close cases above.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The event payload includes the moved editor, the new callback discards it, and the complete synchronous serialization chain is directly visible. The exact serialized byte size depends on editor types, but the per-editor work and unnecessary trigger are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Editor serializer CPU, serialized editor-state strings, and the retained chat-part snapshot
Findings.PerformanceScaling: A move of any tab out of the chat's group serializes every serializable editor in every chat-part group; cost and allocated bytes grow with total open tabs and their serialized state, and repeat for separate tab moves because the microtask guard only coalesces one synchronous batch.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher drag/drop latency, allocation/GC pressure, and a duplicate serialized snapshot retained for the window lifetime
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary editor moves from the chat group did not capture or serialize the complete chat-part state.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new onWillMoveEditor listener ignores the event's editor and target; while the chat remains in the source group it always calls _captureChatPartAsChatLeaves, which stores captureChatPart's full state snapshot.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `_captureChatPartAsChatLeaves(group)` call is registered for every `group.onWillMoveEditor` event, not only for an event whose editor is the chat or whose operation moves the containing group.
Findings.Title: Capture state only when the chat actually leaves
Findings.Impact: Moving a normal tab out of a chat group that also contains the chat synchronously serializes all tabs before the move can complete, even though no restoration snapshot is needed. With many or heavyweight serializable editors this blocks the drop and retains the copied strings until another capture or window disposal.
Findings.Evidence: The added listener checks only `group.contains(content.input)`. Its call reaches captureChatPart -> chatPart.createState -> Grid.serialize -> EditorGroupView.toJSON -> EditorGroupModel.serialize, whose loop calls each editor serializer's canSerialize/serialize. The snapshot is assigned to `_chatPartAsChatLeft`; the queueMicrotask flag merely suppresses repeated captures within the same synchronous group merge.
Findings.Recommendation: Use the move event/editor and a group-leaving signal to capture only when the chat or its group is actually leaving the window; retain the once-per-operation handling for multi-editor merges, and clear/avoid the snapshot when an ordinary sibling tab moves.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The native resize call path and synchronous relayout behavior are explicit in repository code, and the added tests establish the default stacked line has main, chat, and terminal siblings. Exact frame time varies by active editors and number of dropped parts, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous SplitView relayouts and editor-part/DOM layout callbacks
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each native window resize performs one corrective resize for every flexible sibling before the final kept-size resize; with k siblings this adds O(k) whole-line relayouts per resize event, and each relayout walks and lays out affected editor parts.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased synchronous resize cost and dropped frames while dragging or maximizing a populated chat window
Findings.PreviousBehavior: After the grid layout, ChatWindowGrid restored the terminal with one resizeCell call; in the common stacked topology this produced one post-layout height correction.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: PartGrid now restores the proportional shares by calling resizeNode separately for each sibling target and then for the kept terminal, and every resizeNode immediately calls GridView.resizeView.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call `grid.resizeNode([...current.location, index], line.orientation, value)` is reached once for every function in the newly added `steps` loop; before this diff ChatWindowGrid performed a single terminal resize after the main grid layout.
Findings.Title: Batch kept-size corrections into one layout
Findings.Impact: Dragging or maximizing a stacked chat window with terminals visible now performs multiple editor-part layouts for every uncoalesced native resize event. The default main/chat/terminal line already needs two post-layout corrections instead of one, and parts created by edge drops add another correction each, making visible resize increasingly prone to jank.
Findings.Evidence: AuxiliaryWindow registers the native RESIZE event directly to layout(), ChatWindowGrid forwards every event to PartGrid.layout(), and this loop invokes grid.resizeNode once per step. GridView.resizeView calls BranchNode.resizeChild, SplitView.resizeView calls relayout, and relayout/layoutViews synchronously invokes each affected PartGridCell.layout; part cells then call IContentPart.layout and editor layout code.
Findings.Recommendation: Compute the final sibling and terminal sizes together and commit them through one grid/SplitView layout transaction (or encode the fixed terminal plus sibling proportions in the primary layout), preserving the current rounding and constraint behavior without invoking resizeView per sibling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize, drag, maximize, or restore a chat window with the terminal part visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A native auxiliary-window resize event synchronously calls AuxiliaryWindow.layout -> ChatWindowGrid.layout -> PartGrid.layoutGrid -> Grid.layout, followed by kept-size correction before the resize handler returns. The new per-sibling resizeNode calls are therefore on the interactive critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One primary grid layout plus one immediate resize/relayout per sibling correction and one for the kept cell; default stacked layout adds two corrective relayouts, with more for additional direct siblings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: ChatWindowGrid performed the primary layout and one post-layout terminal resize in the common stacked topology rather than correcting each sibling separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All callbacks run synchronously inside the native resize event and can delay the next rendered frame.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resize-event frequency and the number of flexible cells sharing the terminal's row/column after user-created edge-drop parts are included; the default stacked topology has two flexible siblings plus the kept terminal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded and fully serialized. Native resize events are not coalesced here, and each corrective resize completes before the next step/event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: keptShares reuses unrounded proportions only when sibling identities and sizes match, but it does not skip the corrective resize loop; cold and warm paths both perform the synchronous relayouts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: resizeNode reaches GridView.resizeView, SplitView.relayout/layoutViews, PartGridCell.layout, and IContentPart.layout synchronously.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact milliseconds depend on active editor implementations, machine speed, resize event rate, and the number of dropped parts.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous-layout regression; filed as a medium-severity finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move a normal tab, the chat editor, or an entire chat group out of the chat's group/window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before an editor move completes, group.onWillMoveEditor now calls _captureChatPartAsChatLeaves whenever the source group still contains the chat. captureChatPart synchronously creates editor-part state and serializes every serializable editor before the target opens.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the full editor-part grid and every serializable editor input
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full pass over all chat-part groups/editors for every separate editor move from a group containing the chat; serializer output bytes scale with editor state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No chat-part snapshot was created for ordinary per-editor moves.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the editor move/drop completes, adding latency and allocation/GC pressure.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total groups and editors in the chat part and the size/cost of each editor serializer; separate user moves repeat the full work because only callbacks within one microtask are coalesced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous serialization blocks the move. The boolean guard coalesces a same-turn multi-editor merge, but provides no cross-event coalescing or cancellation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no serialization cache. The latest snapshot replaces the previous one, but remains retained even when only a non-chat sibling tab moved and the chat never left.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new listener discards the moved-editor payload, and the full synchronous serialization chain is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor serializer payloads vary substantially; a small tab set is cheap, while many or heavyweight editors amplify the cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable serialization/allocation regression for ordinary sibling-tab moves; filed as a medium-severity finding. Actual chat/group departure still legitimately needs a once-per-operation capture.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close a chat window or reopen it after moving the chat between windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Close first scans all groups in the chat window for move vetoes, then closes/moves editors. Reopen scans for confirmation-requiring editors and serializes only editors that will close before invoking the existing open path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize restorable editor inputs for explicit close/reopen
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one pass over each relevant group/editor per explicit reopen, with dirty/confirmation editors filtered out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same close/reopen workflow already serialized editor state; this diff changes filtering and includes chat-part groups only when required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes close/reopen, but is bounded to the explicit user operation and avoids duplicate dirty editors.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of groups and open editors in the window, including created and terminal parts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Checks and serialization are synchronous and sequential; the subsequent reopen is awaited once. No per-editor subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network fan-out was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Captured chat-part state is reused after the chat leaves; serialized editor lists are temporary. No new cache miss/retry loop exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and cardinality; no external I/O boundary is evidenced in the changed filtering logic.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large tab sets increase explicit reopen cost, but this operation is infrequent and the diff does not increase effective serialization cardinality on the normal reopen path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance finding beyond the over-broad per-tab capture listener.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Changes, Files, Browser, Search, Run, or sidebar shortcuts/menu entries from the main or chat window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Command context resolves the target chat window, then executes exactly one existing tab command or editor-open operation. Browser input creation remains lazy; Search invokes the scoped main-part service once.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One command invocation and one target editor group/window; no collection loop or per-item fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single awaited command/open. No concurrency burst, queue, or missing coalescing mechanism was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser New Tab intentionally uses a fresh UUID and lazy input; other tab behavior uses existing editor/service semantics. No cache key or negative-cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the one-command/one-open delegation shown by the diff and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Downstream editor activation cost depends on editor type, but no changed subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary or multiplicity was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; the changes alter routing and context only.

Scenarios.Scenario: Lay out a proportional SplitView containing a fixed-size view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SplitView.layout already walks all view items; the new clamp executes inline during that existing pass before the normal layoutViews call.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of views in the SplitView, unchanged from the existing linear layout pass.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single layout pass with no added nested relayout or boundary call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing proportions are reused as before; no cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; clamp is constant work per fixed-size item inside an existing traversal.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 30 changed-file patches and traced resize/layout, editor serialization/capture, close/reopen, and command-routing scenarios. Submitted two performance findings: repeated synchronous relayouts during chat-window resize and unnecessary full chat-part serialization on ordinary sibling-tab moves.
